title: Merge k Sorted Lists
source: canonical Merge k Sorted Lists concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is an array of linked lists, each already sorted in ascending order. Merge every list into a single ascending list and return its first node. Lists may be empty, and only the values and their order in the result matter.
constraints: the combined node count stays under 20000

examples.explanation: The three chains weave into one ascending list.

hints: Merging two lists pairwise until one remains works, but early lists get walked over and over.
The next node in the answer is always the smallest front node among all k lists.
Keep the k front nodes in a min-heap: pop the smallest, attach it, push its successor. k exchanges per node total.
solution: Min-heap of the k front nodes: pop the smallest, attach it to the result, and push its successor. Every node passes through the heap once: O(N log k) time for N total nodes, O(k) heap space.
failureHint: hidden tests include a single list, empty lists mixed in, and duplicate values across lists

visible.failNote: always attach the smallest front node
